# Thumbnails and covers

**Covers that read at thumbnail size: the still, the type, the crops, the checks — in Claudia's editorial look.**

Designs thumbnails and covers that get tapped — YouTube thumbnails (1280×720), Shorts frame picks, Reels covers (1080×1920 with the 3:4 profile-grid crop), TikTok covers and X/feed stills — in Claudia's brand (Barlow Condensed uppercase, DM Mono labels, near-black, off-white ink, one rose accent). Covers prompting the cover still itself (face big, eyes to lens, negative space for text) across Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX.2 and Midjourney, adding text in edit with licensed fonts via a tested HTML + headless-Chrome renderer, crop and legibility checks, series systems and A/B testing with YouTube Test & Compare. Use when a short or video needs a cover, when covers look cluttered or get cropped, or when building a recognisable series look.

## How it works

1. Pick the format and its safe area
2. Make (or pick) the still — face big, eyes to lens, room for type
3. Set the type in her look
4. Check crops and legibility
5. Build a series system
6. Test
7. Write alt text

The full instructions are in **[SKILL.md](SKILL.md)**: when to use it, what you need, every step, the checks before you
finish, and the pitfalls.

## Install

```sh
# Claude Code (all projects on this machine)
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
curl -fsSLo /tmp/thumbnails-and-covers.zip https://useclaudia.xyz/skills/thumbnails-and-covers.zip
unzip -oq /tmp/thumbnails-and-covers.zip -d ~/.claude/skills

# Codex and other agents that read ~/.agents/skills
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && unzip -oq /tmp/thumbnails-and-covers.zip -d ~/.agents/skills
```

Or straight from GitHub with the [`skills` CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills):
`npx skills add claudia-onchain/Claudia-Skills --skill thumbnails-and-covers`.

In the Claude apps: **Customize → Skills → + → Upload a skill**, and pick `thumbnails-and-covers.zip` (don't unzip it).
More apps: [install a skill](../../../README.md#install-a-skill).

Then ask for the task in your own words, or call it directly with `/thumbnails-and-covers`.
